page: Google Cloud Platform n4d-highmem-4 is a memory-optimized virtual machine instance featuring 4 dedicated vCPUs and 32.0 GB of system memory. Powered by an x86_64 AMD EPYC 9B45 processor, the instance allocates 2 physical cores with 2 threads per core. The CPU configuration includes a 32 MB L3 cache, 1.0 MB L2 cache, and 48 KB L1d cache. It supports advanced instruction sets such as AVX-512 and cryptographic acceleration via AES and SHA_NI. This instance does not include local storage or bundled GPUs.

Benchmark data reveals strong single-core capabilities, with stress-ng single-core CPU performance, single-threaded gzip compression, and Geekbench single-core scores all placing in the top 10% tier. However, multi-core and memory bandwidth metrics generally fall within the middle 50% average. For instance, the Geekbench multi-core score is 5758.0, and uncached memory read bandwidth is 39.72 GB/sec. Multi-threaded bzip3 decompression is a notable bottleneck, registering in the bottom 25% tier.

Given its 1:8 vCPU-to-RAM ratio, the instance offers memory density suitable for memory-bound workloads that do not require massive parallel processing. It performs adequately for database operations, static web serving, and lightweight language model inference on small models, though medium-sized model inference is poor. The hardware profile provides a cost-efficient option for memory-intensive applications requiring strong single-thread performance without the overhead of high vCPU counts.
description: Google Cloud Platform n4d-highmem-4 is a memory-optimized instance configured with 4 dedicated vCPUs and 32.0 GB of RAM, yielding an 8.0 GB per core ratio. It is powered by an x86_64 AMD EPYC 9B45 processor with 2 physical cores, 2 threads per core, and a 32 MB L3 cache. The instance lacks local storage and GPU accelerators. Performance benchmarks show top-tier single-core execution, including stress-ng single-core and single-threaded gzip compression. Conversely, multi-core benchmarks, memory bandwidth, and database operations align with mid-tier averages, while multi-threaded decompression and medium-sized LLM inference show weaker results. This instance is appropriate for memory-sensitive, single-thread-heavy workloads, such as small-scale database operations, text processing, and static web serving, offering a balanced resource profile without the cost of unnecessary CPU cores.
